Qt 6.12.0 source and replacement

The Editor uses unmodified Qt Core, Gui, Widgets and qwindows.dll through dynamic linking, under LGPL version 3.
Qt is copyright The Qt Company Ltd. and other contributors. License texts and third-party notices are in licenses/Qt-NOTICES.txt.
gEngine's own license does not replace these third-party licenses.

Corresponding source (Qt Base, including bundled third-party code and build scripts):
https://download.qt.io/official_releases/qt/6.12/6.12.0/submodules/qtbase-everywhere-src-6.12.0.tar.xz
SHA-256: a951bd163c7b80fc6b8c88d7668fb56abf91c152373e13c10666763238131307
Upstream source commit: 025bdad181de241e81bf853c8a2d7bf3d19261a9
The source is also placed in Sources/ when GENGINE_QT_SOURCE_ARCHIVE is configured.
Binary distributors must provide this corresponding source with the binary download, or equivalent access from the same place. Do not rely solely on a third-party link remaining available.

Replacement: close the Editor, preserve the current DLLs, and replace Qt6Core.dll, Qt6Gui.dll, Qt6Widgets.dll and platforms/qwindows.dll together with an ABI-compatible Windows x64 MSVC dynamic Qt build. Both gEngine Debug and Release use Qt release DLLs to match the shared /MD CRT required by the Rust runtime. Do not substitute debug DLLs ending in d. qt.conf keeps plugin lookup relative to this Editor directory. No signature or hash check prevents replacement.
Rebuilding Qt: use the included source's configure script, an x64 MSVC environment and CMake. Configure a shared build with the same compiler ABI and configuration, then build and install Core/Gui/Widgets and the Windows platform plugin. The original binary build options are recorded in the installed Qt Base SBOM.
Modification of Qt and reverse engineering for debugging such modifications are permitted under the applicable LGPL terms. There is no gEngine restriction on those activities.
